methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates ctDNA, WES/RNA-seq, Ba/F3 isogenic models with site-directed mutagenesis, PDXs, and structural analyses, which is a design well matched to the question of resistance mechanisms. Preclinical rigor includes WT FGFR2::BICC1 controls, Sanger confirmation of mutants, and 6 mice/group PDX studies, but the methods explicitly note cells were not tested for Mycoplasma, and PDX randomization/blinded tumor measurement are not described. Statistically, a permutation chi-square test (P<1×10^-5) is used to compare mutation spectra and GSEA uses Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, but IC50 fold-changes are reported without confidence intervals or replicate counts, and no power calculation is provided for the clinical cohort. Three different ctDNA panels with different VAF thresholds introduce acknowledged technical heterogeneity; comparison with futibatinib resistance relies on a historical/published cohort rather than contemporaneous controls.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The clinical evidence consists of a translational case series/single-institution cohort of 30 patients from the ReFocus trial with molecular correlative analyses, and the sequential-treatment efficacy claim rests on only three patients (one of whom is counted from a prior publication), consistent with Oxford LoE 4 (case series/low-quality cohort). Despite this, clinical relevance is high because the findings directly inform sequencing of two clinically available/approvable irreversible FGFR2 inhibitors (futibatinib approved; lirafugratinib expected 2026-2027), identify actionable ctDNA biomarkers (M538I/L618F vs N550/V565), and are supported by congruent mechanistic, cellular, in vivo (PDX), and structural data. Endpoints include clinical benefit and radiologic response in real patients, with a plausible path to practice-informing recommendations in FGFR2-driven cholangiocarcinoma and tumor-agnostic settings.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the closest applicable standard given the biomarker/resistance-mutation focus, with elements of ARRIVE for the PDX work and STROBE for the observational cohort. Strengths include registration of three parent studies (NCT04526106, NCT04932525, NCT02517892), explicit case definitions for primary vs acquired resistance (BOR/PFS<6 months per Jackman 2010), transcript nomenclature clarification, and transparent limitations. However, there is no CONSORT/STROBE-style flow diagram, inclusion/exclusion criteria for the UNLOCK-03 subset are not fully enumerated, antibody/assay validation and ARRIVE items (randomization, blinding, exclusion criteria for mice) are incomplete, and no data-availability statement, repository accession, or code repository is evident in the blinded text—raw ctDNA/WES/RNA-seq data access terms are not specified.

novelty_literature.justification: The study provides the first systematic clinical description of the FGFR2 M538I/L618F mutational hotspot pattern as a dominant on-target resistance mechanism specifically to lirafugratinib (69% of acquired resistance cases), distinct from the N550/V565 pattern associated with futibatinib (empirical and mechanistic novelty). The combination of mutational cataloguing, isogenic cellular validation, PDX cross-validation, structural rationale (open vs closed kinase conformation; van der Waals contact with M538, hydrophobic network with L618/F646), and clinical sequence proof-of-concept constitutes a cohesive novel contribution. Novelty is appropriately bounded: the futibatinib comparator derives from Goyal 2025 (ref 24) rather than new primary data, and the authors' own prior work (ref 13, Facchinetti 2024) already established the complementary futibatinib→lirafugratinib direction, so the current manuscript extends rather than inaugurates the sequencing paradigm.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a logical progression from cohort description through resistance stratification, cross-inhibitor comparison, cellular/PDX validation, structural rationale, and sequential clinical cases. The abstract is quantitatively grounded (30 patients, 11/16 with M538/L618 mutations, three sequence patients) and faithfully summarizes the findings. Figure captions are informative and standalone-interpretable, with transcript nomenclature carefully clarified to prevent reader confusion (M538 vs M537). Minor weaknesses include some repetition between Results and Discussion of the N550/V565 vs M538/L618 contrast, a few awkward constructions (e.g., 'on difference alleles'), and a 'Figure 1..' double-period typo.

key_strengths: Clinically actionable discovery of M538I/L618F as dominant lirafugratinib resistance hotspots (11/16, 69%) with mechanistic complementarity to futibatinib N550/V565 vulnerabilities
Multi-modal convergent evidence: patient ctDNA/WES/RNA-seq, isogenic Ba/F3 IC50 and signaling assays, three concordant PDX models, and structural rationale from PDB 8STG/8W2X
Rigorous permutation-based comparison of mutation spectra (P<1×10^-5) across lirafugratinib and the published futibatinib cohort (Goyal 2025)
Direct translational payoff: three patients demonstrating durable futibatinib response after lirafugratinib progression, with ctDNA tracking of resistant clones
Transparent, specific limitations section addressing genetic-only focus, panel heterogeneity, and single-mutation PDXs
key_concerns: Clinical sequence evidence rests on only three patients (and one is cited from prior publication), limiting the strength of the practice-informing claim
No data-availability statement, repository accession, or analytical code shared in the blinded text; raw ctDNA/WES/RNA-seq access terms not specified

Preclinical reporting gaps: Mycoplasma testing not performed (acknowledged), PDX randomization/blinded measurement not described, IC50 values lack CIs and replicate counts, antibody validation incomplete
Three different ctDNA panels with heterogeneous VAF thresholds introduce technical variability in the primary mutation calls
Comparator for futibatinib resistance is a historical published cohort rather than contemporaneous same-platform data
GSEA findings on 'hallmark' enrichments are underpowered and appropriately caveated but may still over-interpret small-n RNA-seq subsets
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a cohesive, mechanistically rigorous translational study with a novel and clinically actionable finding (differential kinase-domain mutational landscape across two irreversible FGFR2 inhibitors enabling rational sequencing), supported by concordant clinical, cellular, in vivo, and structural data—placing it within Tier 1 scope (e.g., Cancer Discovery/Annals of Oncology range). Minor revisions are warranted to address data/code availability, add CIs/replicates to IC50 data, and more cautiously frame the n=3 clinical sequencing evidence.
